requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The installed root cron entry has the exact daily 02:15 schedule, and crond was active and enabled both before and after restart. A cron-like execution also demonstrated that the command runs successfully in the configured minimal environment.

The cron entry appends stdout and stderr to the requested log. Direct executions increased the log from zero to one line and then from one to two lines; the first line remained present across a verified node restart. Final file evidence shows a root-owned log with mode 0644 and the var_log_t SELinux context.

overall_summary: Both contractual outcomes are satisfied. The independent restart protocol is complete: node1 had a pre-restart boot identity and healthy scheduler/task state, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot identity was observed afterward and independently confirmed by lifecycle evidence, and the scheduler, cron entry, retained log data, and command output recovered successfully.
limitations: No naturally timed 02:15 cron invocation was captured; scheduling is established by the exact cron entry, active/enabled crond service, and successful cron-like executions.
Package-health collection timed out in both lifecycle snapshots, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.

The node clock changed substantially across the restart, producing an August timestamp before restart and an October timestamp afterward; this does not contradict the demonstrated append behavior or persistence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing mutations were identified. Creating and labeling the cron and log files directly implemented the task; the two manual executions were bounded functional evidence; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The initial unprivileged write failed before creating the cron file, while the unsupported crond -T check was diagnostic and shows no mutation. No failed services, new exposures, or executor-created temporary residue were observed after completion.
